official.deadline_note: Perimeter publishes no fixed central deadline. The official How to Apply page states the Expression of Interest deadline is based on the application deadline of the partner university you apply to, and that the Expression of Interest must be submitted within one week of submitting the university application (using the earliest application date if you apply to several universities). Perimeter's Expression of Interest posting for the 2027 award lists the application deadline as 'none'.
official.application_cycle: 2027 Expression of Interest for PhD Residency Award (posted 13 August 2026), for a Fall start; official submission window is November to January for a September start
official.status_note: The official How to Apply page publishes the live application steps and links the Expression of Interest posting, which is open for the 2027 award and carries no fixed deadline. The official timeline runs November-January (university application plus Expression of Interest), February-March (universities issue offer letters), April-May (Perimeter contacts selected students), August-September (arrival in Waterloo).
official.tuition_coverage_note: Perimeter states the top-up is 'Top-up funding to $30,000 per year (after fees and tuition) until Term 12' and that it 'builds on the university department's standard funding package', so fees and tuition are settled before the top-up is calculated. Resident PhD students 'are financially supported through their home university (typically for 4 years / 12 academic terms)'. Perimeter does not state that it pays tuition.

application_method: STEP 1: search the researcher list on the official How to Apply page for the Faculty or Senior Researcher you want to supervise your PhD
STEP 2: follow their 'Apply To' link to begin the partner-university application, and review that university's own application requirements and deadlines
STEP 3: submit your Expression of Interest to the PhD Residency Program Award (via AcademicJobsOnline) within one week of submitting your university application
STEP 4: when the partner-university offer letter arrives, upload it to your Expression of Interest application
Perimeter then contacts selected students in April-May; students commit to a university programme and start date and arrive in Waterloo in August-September
official.application_route: Apply to a partner university's PhD programme first, then submit the Perimeter Expression of Interest within one week of that university application, and upload the university offer letter when it arrives.
official.study_mode: Full-time (resident PhD students are expected to make the Institute their main base of research)
official.international_eligibility: No citizenship or residency restriction is published for the Residency Award; eligibility turns on admission to a partner-university PhD programme and supervision by a Perimeter-affiliated Faculty, Associate Faculty or Senior Researcher.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Theoretical physics and closely allied fields. The official researcher list is organised by Cosmology, Mathematical Physics, Particle Physics, Quantum Fields and Strings, Quantum Foundations, Quantum Gravity, Quantum Information, Quantum Matter, Strong Gravity and Computational Physics; the Expression of Interest posting lists Theoretical Physics / Gravity, Quantum Information, Cosmology, Quantum Field Theory, Quantum Gravity, Quantum Information Theory, Quantum information/quantum matter, String theory, Theoretical condensed matter physics and Theoretical particle physics.
official.research_requirement: A Statement of Purpose (2 pages max) in the Expression of Interest; research fit with a listed Perimeter supervisor is central, and the award also requires acceptance by a Perimeter faculty member to work in their group.
official.duration: Typically 4 years / 12 academic terms; the top-up runs until Term 12 on a September-August academic year
official.description: Perimeter Institute offers resident PhD students an environment to interact with research leaders while laying the foundation for a career in physics. Resident PhD students are supervised by Perimeter Faculty, Associate Faculty or a Senior Researcher but take their degree from a partnering university, and are financially supported through their home university, typically for 4 years / 12 academic terms, in addition to the PhD Residency Program Award.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an add-on to a partner-university PhD, not a standalone scholarship: you first have to win a place on a PhD programme at Dalhousie, McMaster, Guelph, Toronto, Waterloo, Western or York with a supervisor who also holds a Perimeter appointment. Your income target is $30,000 per year after fees and tuition, layered on the home department's standard package, plus a $2,000 technology grant and a desk at the Institute. Plan the paperwork around the university's own application deadline, because your Perimeter Expression of Interest has to land within one week of it, and no residency promise is possible before the university's offer letter exists. Start early on the supervisor relationship, since the award also requires the faculty member to agree to take you into their group.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A theoretically minded physicist or mathematician targeting a Canadian PhD with a specifically named Perimeter supervisor, who is comfortable running two applications in parallel.
application_readiness_checklist: Pick 3-5 named Perimeter supervisors from the official researcher list and confirm each one's affiliated university department before writing to anyone
Check each target department's own application deadline and work backwards: your Expression of Interest is due within one week of the earliest university application you submit
Line up three or four referees who will upload letters themselves through the Expression of Interest portal, and ask them months before you need them
Draft a Statement of Purpose that fits the hard 2-page limit and speaks to specific supervisor research
Keep transcripts and optional ELP scores ready so the Expression of Interest itself is never the bottleneck
Budget for the Waterloo arrival in August-September: housing, a Canadian study permit and relocation are all on you
common_rejection_risks: Treating the Expression of Interest as the PhD application: Perimeter states explicitly that it is NOT an application to a PhD programme, and skipping the separate university application ends the bid
Supervisor silence - the official FAQ acknowledges researchers receive many emails and cannot answer them all, so an unanswered email is not a soft yes
Missing the one-week window between the university application and the Expression of Interest, especially if you apply to several universities and miss that the earliest date governs
Expecting a residency decision before the university offer; Perimeter states a formal offer of residency cannot be made until after the university offer is made
Assuming the top-up is the whole package and ignoring the home department's funding, which is what the $30,000 figure builds on
Underestimating the Canadian master's-before-PhD convention, which the official page flags for applicants familiar with the US system
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and fees are handled by the home-university package, not by Perimeter. You still fund airfare and relocation to Waterloo, a Canadian study permit and visa fees, and day-to-day living. Perimeter's own visiting-student page publishes Waterloo estimates of roughly $750-$1,200 per month for housing plus utilities, about $600 for food and about $385 in personal expenses, i.e. roughly $1,800-$2,200 per month - a useful benchmark for what the university package plus top-up must absorb.
document_audit: Statement of Purpose has a strict 2-page maximum, so it must be a tight research pitch rather than a general statement
Three to four reference letters are submitted online by the referees themselves, so the application is not complete until they act - chase them early and confirm uploads
The university offer letter is uploaded after you submit, so do not delay the Expression of Interest waiting for it
Transcripts: a post-secondary degree transcript is required and further post-secondary transcripts are optional, so declare every institution you attended
ELP results (TOEFL, IELTS, C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency) are optional in the portal but are the cheapest way to pre-empt any doubt about English proficiency
alerts: One Expression of Interest covers up to five Faculty or Senior Researchers across all partner universities, so never file one per university
Where you apply to several universities, the earliest application date sets your one-week Expression of Interest deadline
The residency start date is generally tied to the Fall intake cycle, with mid-year exceptions only possible - do not plan a January arrival
Universities issue offers only in February-March and Perimeter contacts successful students in April-May, so visa and housing work happens late in a tight window before an August-September start
Perimeter offers support and accommodations throughout the application process for applicants with disabilities - request it early rather than late
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Two parallel submissions: the partner-university PhD application on its own portal and timeline, then the Perimeter Expression of Interest within one week of that application; the university offer letter is uploaded afterwards, and Perimeter makes its selections in April-May for an August-September start.

official.deadline_note: Direct exchange applicants must meet their home institution's internal deadline, which is earlier than January 31. Fulbright Canada states that all partner institutions have internal deadlines and advises applicants to identify the date their institution's internal competition ends via a study abroad advisor.
official.application_cycle: 2027-28 Killam Fellowships competition; competition opened August 15, 2026, for placement in Fall or Spring of the next school year
official.status_note: The Fulbright Canada programme pages state 'COMPETITION OPEN on AUGUST 15, 2026' and that the deadline for the open competition for the 2027-28 Killam Fellowships competition is January 31, 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Killam does not pay tuition. Direct exchange students register at their home university, pay their home fees, and attend the host university as an exchange visitor; self-placed visiting students register at the host university and pay host tuition fees.
benefits: Cash award of $6,000 US for a one-semester exchange, or $12,000 US for the full academic year
Health benefit plan provided to American Killam Fellows; the Canadian pages state the Foundation provides all Killam Fellows with a health benefit plan
Three-day Fall Orientation in Ottawa, ON and a three-day Spring Seminar in Washington, D.C.

Mobility (in-country travel) grant in an amount not to exceed $800 - listed as C$800 on the American award provisions page and as $800 US on the Canadian award provisions page - on a competitive basis, to be taken up during the exchange period
Eligibility to apply for a $5,000 Killam Community Action Initiative Grant, open to grantees and alumni
Eligibility for paid internship opportunities for alumni through the Fulbright Canada Alumni Internship Program, plus the Local Ambassador Program matching current grantees with Killam alumni
eligibility: Canadian applicants must be Canadian citizens; American applicants must be U.S. citizens

Full-time undergraduate students in good standing at a degree-granting institution in their home country (the American page specifies a fully accredited degree-granting college or university in the United States), who have met their home university's eligibility requirements relating to participation in international exchange programmes
Expect to receive an undergraduate degree in the Spring of 2028 or beyond
Be fluent in the English language (and/or French, where appropriate)
Have a superior and competitive academic record, and complete the application process prior to the published deadlines
Direct exchange applicants must be nominated by their home university
requirements: Choose the direct exchange route or the open competition - there is a single application form for all applicants

Direct exchange: be registered and in good standing at a participating university and be planning to take up the award at a participating university in the other country; participating universities may nominate up to three full-year candidates (or six one-semester candidates)

Open competition: be currently enrolled at any degree-granting institution in the home country (including participating universities) and apply to any degree-granting institution in the other country; submit by January 31
All awards are subject to the availability of funds, acceptance by the host university, and the ability to secure appropriate visa arrangements
Direct exchange applicants must meet their home institution's internal deadline; open competition applicants must meet January 31
documents: Proof of Citizenship (pdf, 1 page, passport preferred) and Curriculum Vitae (pdf, up to 3 pages, 12 point font, 1" margins)
Unofficial transcript(s) from all post-secondary education institutions (pdf)
Personal Statement (pdf, 1 page, single spaced, 12 point font, 1" margins)
Supplementary Document Package Cover Form (pdf, 1 page, to be filled out by your student advisor), and a request for 2 references filled out in the application form

Course Selection Forms (pdf, 1 page) - one per institution, signed by an official at your home institution; direct exchange applicants need only their top 3 picks, open competition applicants up to 3 institutions
Letter(s) of Acceptance (pdf) if applying to the open competition and you have already received one
selection_criteria: Ranking by an independent adjudication committee of faculty members from participating universities and senior Foundation officials
coverage: Cash award of $6,000 US per semester or $12,000 US for the full academic year
Three-day Fall Orientation in Ottawa and a three-day Spring Seminar in Washington, D.C.
Competitive mobility (in-country travel) grant of up to $800 for an educational field trip during the exchange period
Eligibility for a $5,000 Killam Community Action Initiative Grant and the Fulbright Canada Alumni Internship Program
application_method: Decide between the direct exchange programme (nominated by your home institution) and the open competition (apply directly to any degree-granting institution in the other country); there is a single application form
Prepare the published document package, including the advisor-completed Supplementary Document Package Cover Form and signed Course Selection Forms
Submit through the Fulbright Canada Apply Now page by your home institution's internal deadline (direct exchange) or by January 31 (open competition)
Fill out the request for 2 references in the application form so referees can submit
official.application_route: One online application on Fulbright Canada's Apply Now page - direct exchange applicants must first win their home institution's nomination, open competition applicants apply directly by January 31.
official.study_mode: Full-time undergraduate exchange, one semester or a full academic year
official.citizenship_residency: Canadian applicants must be Canadian citizens; American applicants must be U.S. citizens.
official.international_eligibility: The programme is itself a binational Canada-United States exchange. Canadians must study in the United States and Americans in Canada: direct exchange applicants must go from a participating university in one country to a participating university in the other, while open competition applicants may go from any degree-granting institution to any degree-granting institution in the other country.
official.duration: One semester or a full academic year
official.description: The Killam Fellowships Program provides an opportunity for exceptional undergraduate students from universities in Canada and the United States to spend either one semester or a full academic year as an exchange student in the other country, either as a direct exchange student or as a self-placed visiting student. The Foundation hosts all new Fellows at an Orientation in Ottawa each fall and at a seminar in Washington, D.C. each spring.
official.region: North America (Canada and the United States)

applicant_utility.summary: This is a stipend for a semester or year abroad, not a tuition scholarship: US$6,000 per semester or US$12,000 for the year, with a health plan, an Ottawa orientation, a Washington spring seminar and a chance at an $800 in-country travel grant. You must be an undergraduate at a Canadian or American university who will not graduate before Spring 2028, and the exchange must run Canada-to-US or US-to-Canada. The single biggest scheduling risk is not the January 31 open-competition deadline but your own campus's internal nomination deadline, which comes first. Decide early whether you go as a direct exchange student paying home fees or as a self-placed visiting student paying host tuition, because that choice determines whether your bank account or your home transcript absorbs the cost.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A high-achieving undergraduate at a Canadian or American partner university who wants a funded semester or year across the border and can meet their own institution's internal nomination deadline.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm with your study abroad office the date your institution's internal Killam competition closes, and work backwards from that instead of from January 31
Check the Spring 2028-or-later degree rule against your own graduation plan before investing effort
Identify the participating universities you want and get the corresponding Course Selection Forms signed by an official at your home institution
Ask your student advisor early to complete the Supplementary Document Package Cover Form - it is a one-page third-party dependency that stalls applications
Trigger the two reference requests inside the application form as soon as you open it, not at the end
Model the true cost: as a direct exchange student you keep paying home tuition, as a self-placed visiting student you pay host tuition out of the US$6,000-US$12,000 stipend
common_rejection_risks: Missing the home institution's internal deadline for the direct exchange route - Fulbright Canada states all partner institutions have internal deadlines, and every one of them falls before January 31
Graduating too soon: the published rule requires an undergraduate degree in Spring 2028 or beyond, which quietly excludes final-year students in the current cycle
Applying to the open competition but naming only partner institutions, or the reverse - assuming a nomination that the route does not provide
Award conditionality: all awards are subject to availability of funds, acceptance by the host university, and securing appropriate visa arrangements, so a strong file can still fail at the host stage
A file that is competitive on grades but thin on the proposed programme of study and personal statement, which the adjudication committee ranks explicitly alongside academic record and references
An incomplete document package - unsigned course selection forms or a missing advisor cover form are administrative failures, not judgement calls
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition in every case: home fees as a direct exchange student, host tuition as a self-placed visiting student. You also fund international airfare, visa and immigration costs, and general living costs in the host country, since the only travel support is the competitive mobility grant of up to $800 (listed as C$800 on the American provisions page and $800 US on the Canadian provisions page), which must be used for an educational field trip during the exchange.
document_audit: Proof of citizenship must be a single page, and Fulbright Canada prefers a passport - a driver's licence or birth certificate copy may not read as official proof
The CV has a 3-page ceiling at 12 point font with 1-inch margins, so a research CV with publications must be cut deliberately
Unofficial transcripts are required from every post-secondary institution attended, including transfer and exchange credit - omit one and the file looks incomplete
The Personal Statement is a single-spaced page at 12 point, so it has to carry the proposed programme of study argument with no room for padding

The Supplementary Document Package Cover Form is filled out by your student advisor, not by you, and the Course Selection Forms need a home-institution official's signature - both depend on someone else's calendar
alerts: The competition opened August 15, 2026, so the January 31, 2027 open-competition deadline is a hard date, not a rolling one
Direct exchange nominations are capped at three full-year or six one-semester candidates per partner university, so competition for your campus's slots is internal and early
Applications are for placement in Fall or Spring of the next school year, so a missed cycle costs a full year
New Fellows are expected at the fall orientation in Ottawa, and there is a spring seminar in Washington, D.C. - factor both into your term and travel plans
The stipend is US$6,000 for a semester and US$12,000 for the year; do not budget the year figure for a one-semester placement
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online application on Fulbright Canada's Apply Now page, uploaded with the advisor-signed and officially-signed forms plus two references; direct exchange files are screened and nominated by the home institution first, then an independent adjudication committee of partner-university faculty and Foundation officials ranks all candidates and produces a recommended list including alternates.
